claim.pdf_says: '14.2.3   General rules' is printed as a fourth-level clause heading, a sibling of '14.2.1   General formats' (page 557) and '14.2.2   Syntax rules' (page 558), all children of '14.2   Procedure division structure'.
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.2.3 General rules   (while its sibling on page 557 is '#### 14.2.1 General formats' and its parent is '### 14.2 Procedure division structure')
claim.why_it_matters: The heading is emitted two levels ABOVE its parent, so in the rendered outline 14.2.3 becomes a peer of clause 14 rather than a child of 14.2. Any TOC generator or anchor-driven lookup over the transcription mis-nests every general rule in 14.2.3 (the rules governing USING/RETURNING parameter passing) out of the procedure-division-structure subtree.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The claimed kind is 'missing-heading', but the heading is present, verbatim and correctly numbered. Rendered page 559 prints exactly '14.2.3 General rules'; the transcription carries '## 14.2.3 General rules' (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23390; page-559.md line 29), immediately preceded by a correct anchor '' (line 23389). Both the clause number and the title text match the printed page character-for-character. No spec content -- no syntax rule, general rule, or format -- is lost, moved, or altered on this page. (2) THE PDF CARRIES NO HEADING-LEVEL INFORMATION FOR THE MARKDOWN TO CONTRADICT. I rendered page 557 at 300 dpi and looked at the printed glyphs directly. '14 Procedure division', '14.1 General', '14.2 Procedure division structure' and '14.2.1 General formats' are set in the IDENTICAL bold typeface, at the IDENTICAL point size, flush to the IDENTICAL left margin -- there is no size step, no indent step, no rule, no numbering-style change between a clause, a subclause and a sub-subclause. ISO encodes nesting depth SOLELY in the dotted clause number. The transcription preserves that number ('14.2.3') intact, therefore it preserves 100% of the depth information the PDF actually contains. The markdown '#' count is the transcriber's own presentation metadata with no counterpart in the source document, so there is no PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy here -- only a markdown styling choice. (3) THE CLAIM MISDESCRIBES BOTH SOURCES. It calls 14.2.3 'a fourth-level clause heading'; a three-component number (14 . 2 . 3) is a THIRD-level heading. It also asserts that 14.2.2 on page 558 is a properly-nested sibling that 14.2.3 breaks away from; in fact the transcription emits '## 14.2.2 Syntax rules' (line 23341) at the SAME '##' depth as 14.2.3, and emits the following subclause as '## 14.3 Declaratives' (line 23492) at '##' as well. 14.2.3 is not an outlier against its neighbours -- it matches them. The genuine local outlier is '#### 14.2.1' (line 23269), the only '####' in the neighbourhood. (4) THERE IS NO CONSISTENT CONVENTION TO VIOLATE, AND THE STATED HARM IS FALSE. Measured across the whole transcription, three-component clause headings are emitted at '###' 508 times, at '##' 276 times, and at '####' 17 times; two-component headings at '##' 192 times and '###' only 35 times. So '## 14.2.3' follows the second-most-common pattern while its supposedly-correct parent '### 14.2' follows a 35-of-227 minority pattern. Heading depth in this transcription is uniformly unreliable document-wide (an artifact of inferring level from font size in a document that does not vary font size by level); singling out page 559 as a discrete structural defect is not supportable -- it would be one arbitrary instance of ~276. Finally, the claimed consequence is factually wrong on its own terms: anchor-driven lookup resolves through '#section-14-2-3', which is present and correct, so anchor lookup is entirely unaffected. Only a hypothetical TOC generator keying off '#' depth would nest oddly, and it would do so identically for 14.2.2 and 14.3 -- i.e. this is a global formatting property of the transcription, not a page-559 content discrepancy. Per the rejection criteria: the 'missing' text is present, the difference is formatting-only, the claim misquotes both sources, and no meaning changes. Verdict: not a real discrepancy.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The heading '14.2.3 General rules' is present verbatim in the transcription with a correct '' anchor; nothing is missing. The PDF sets clause, subclause and sub-subclause headings (14, 14.1, 14.2, 14.2.1) in one identical bold face, size and margin, carrying depth only in the dotted number -- which the transcription preserves exactly. The sole difference is the markdown '#' nesting depth, transcriber-added metadata with no source counterpart, and it is inconsistent document-wide (three-component headings: 508x '###', 276x '##', 17x '####'), not specific to this page. The claim additionally misstates the facts: 14.2.3 is a third-level, not fourth-level, heading; its page-558 sibling 14.2.2 is emitted at the SAME '##' depth (as is the following 14.3), so 14.2.3 is not an outlier against its neighbours; and anchor-driven lookup is unaffected because the anchor is correct. If any cleanup is ever wanted it is a global, cosmetic heading-depth normalization pass over the whole file, not a page-559 spec-fidelity fix.
